## About this page

*Only in the desktop app.*

Lets ssh, git and other programs use the SSH keys in your vault while it is open, with nothing on disk.

#### Why it is there

A private key in a file can be copied by anything that reads your home folder. Kept in the vault, it is encrypted when the vault is locked and answers only while it is open.

#### How it works

WM Pass speaks the part of the SSH agent protocol that programs need: listing keys, and signing with them. Programs find it through SSH\_AUTH\_SOCK, the line under [Point your shell at it](/guide/settings/ssh/#action-ssh-shell).

The private key never leaves WM Pass. A program sends what it needs signed and gets back only the signature.

See also [The SSH agent](/guide/how-it-works/#feature-ssh), [Run the SSH agent](/guide/settings/ssh/#setting-ssh-agent), [Ask before each use](/guide/settings/ssh/#setting-ssh-confirm).

<a id="setting-ssh-agent"></a>

## Run the SSH agent

*Only in the desktop app.*

Starts an SSH agent inside WM Pass that offers the keys in your vault.

#### How it works

On macOS and Linux it listens on a socket in a folder only your user account can enter. On Windows it is the named pipe \\\\.\\pipe\\wmpass-ssh-agent.

A key is offered when its item has **Offer to the SSH agent** turned on. Keys in the trash or on the hidden shelf are not offered.

When the vault locks, the agent has nothing to offer. It answers again once you unlock.

#### Limits

It does not take keys from ssh-add. Add keys as items in the vault.

It signs only with Ed25519 keys. An RSA or ECDSA key kept in the vault is listed to programs, but a request to sign with it fails.

Any program running as you can ask for the list of public keys. With [Ask before each use](/guide/settings/ssh/#setting-ssh-confirm) off, it can also have them sign without asking.

See also [Ask before each use](/guide/settings/ssh/#setting-ssh-confirm), [Point your shell at it](/guide/settings/ssh/#action-ssh-shell), [Keys in this vault](/guide/settings/ssh/#group-ssh-keys).

<a id="setting-ssh-confirm"></a>

## Ask before each use

*Only in the desktop app.*

Shows a window each time a program wants one of your keys to sign something, naming the key, with **Allow** and **Refuse**.

#### Why it is there

Without it, any program running as you can use your keys while the vault is open, such as to sign in to your servers or push to your repositories, and you would not know.

#### What each choice does

| Choice | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| On | Every signature waits for your answer. Listing the keys does not ask. |
| Off | Programs sign with any offered key while the vault is open, without a question. |

#### Limits

The window cannot tell you which program is asking. If you did not run ssh or git yourself a moment ago, refuse.

A settings file cannot turn this off.

See also [Run the SSH agent](/guide/settings/ssh/#setting-ssh-agent).

<a id="action-ssh-shell"></a>

## Point your shell at it

*Only in the desktop app.*

The line that tells ssh and git where the agent is. Copy it and run it in a terminal.

#### How it works

It sets SSH\_AUTH\_SOCK for that terminal only. To keep it, add the line to your shell's startup file, such as ~/.zshrc or ~/.bashrc, or to your PowerShell profile on Windows.

#### Limits

Shown only while the agent is running.

See also [Run the SSH agent](/guide/settings/ssh/#setting-ssh-agent).

<a id="group-ssh-keys"></a>

## Keys in this vault

*Only in the desktop app.*

Every SSH key item in the open vault. Click one to open it.

#### How it works

Make a new key from the New item menu. Only Ed25519 keys are generated here; other keys can be pasted in as OpenSSH text. A key with a passphrase keeps it in the item, and the agent uses it to sign.

#### Limits

Being listed here is not the same as being offered. A key reaches the agent only with **Offer to the SSH agent** on in its item.

The agent can sign only with an Ed25519 key. Other keys can be kept here, for copying, but not used through the agent.

See also [Run the SSH agent](/guide/settings/ssh/#setting-ssh-agent), [Kinds of item](/guide/how-it-works/#concept-item-kinds).
